corpora.name: human-mc4-shop
corpora.what: Italian product and shop pages: the prose paragraphs of each page (15 or more words, at least 22% Italian function words, few capitalised words), 40 to 900 words, at least two product nouns, at most 2 pages per host, 705 hosts. A page counts as a shop page when its URL path contains /prodotto/, /product/, /shop/, /negozio/, /store/, /catalogo/, /item/ or /p/, or its text says 'aggiungi al carrello'. Known machine-translated marketplaces and Etsy, eBay, Amazon and AliExpress were left out.
corpora.source: mC4 Italian, validation shards 0-7 and train shards 0-3, https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/c4
corpora.license: mC4 is released under ODC-BY 1.0 and the Common Crawl terms of use. The page text belongs to the sites, so only URL, crawl date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.
corpora.caveats: Italian product copy in general (furniture, fashion, cosmetics, stationery), not only gifts and print-on-demand items, and not Etsy. A few pages are machine translations from English that the filter missed.

corpora.name: human-mc4-shop-holdout
corpora.what: The same filter on train shards 4-6, without hosts already in human-mc4-shop (330 hosts). Built after the list was frozen and not used for any decision.

corpora.name: human-mc4-web
corpora.what: A random 1.2% sample (seed 42) of the Italian web: the prose paragraphs of each page (12 or more words), 40 to 1,200 words, spam keywords excluded. A check against ordinary Italian.

corpora.name: desegma-human
corpora.what: A random sample (seed 42) of the human news texts in the Subtask A training file. News, not product copy.
corpora.source: DeSegMa-IT, EVALITA 2026 shared task on machine-generated Italian (Andrea Esuli, Andrea Pedrotti, Giovanni Puccetti, ISTI-CNR), https://desegma.github.io/
corpora.license: Not stated on the task pages, so only row numbers and SHA-256 are shipped. Download the CSV from https://desegma.github.io/data/ to rebuild.
corpora.dates: Not stated by the task; undated here, so not known to be from before November 2022.

corpora.name: human-mc4-web-holdout
corpora.what: 1,000 random pages of the Italian web from a validation shard, URLs already in another Italian corpus excluded: the prose paragraphs of each page (12 or more words, enough function words, few capitals; scripts/lib/prose.mjs), 40 to 1,200 words, spam keywords excluded, drawn by a seeded shuffle (seed 42) by scripts/sample-mc4-web.mjs. Not used for any decision about the existing entries or the general candidates.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.

corpora.name: desegma-machine
corpora.what: A random sample (seed 42) of the machine-written news texts in the same file.
corpora.dates: Not stated by the task; undated here.

corpora.name: ai-models
corpora.what: Titles and descriptions from Claude Sonnet (80), Claude Haiku (80) and Claude Opus (40), answering 120 plain seller requests ('Scrivi la descrizione per il mio prodotto Etsy: tazza…') and 80 requests for a 'descrizione accattivante e persuasiva'. The request is stored with each text. The models were asked to answer as they normally would and saw no pattern list. Exact model versions were not recorded.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only. No ChatGPT, Gemini or Llama output was available, so their register is missing.

corpora.name: ai-imitation
corpora.what: Titles and descriptions generated with Claude in the default listing style of chat assistants (emoji, 'Scopri…', 'Che tu sia… o…').
corpora.caveats: Written with the candidate patterns in view, so hit rates here overstate recall. It shows that the regexes fire on the intended shapes, nothing more.

corpora.name: ai-general
corpora.what: Claude Sonnet (48) and Claude Haiku (48) answering plain requests in six genres (blog post, email to colleagues, short essay, newspaper article, LinkedIn post, short report) on eight everyday topics, made by scripts/generate-general.mjs from scripts/general-requests.json. The models saw no pattern list. The general entries added in 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 were drawn from this set, so its hit rates overstate recall; ai-multi-holdout and ai-detailed-holdout are the clean held-out measure.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only, 96 texts. Claude Code put the account's email address in the context, and Sonnet signed 11 emails across the three languages with the account owner's name; that name was replaced by a neutral one and the rows carry a 'redacted' note. The model ids were not recorded at generation; each row carries the id the alias resolved to with the same CLI version on the same day.

corpora.name: ai-general-holdout
corpora.what: Claude Sonnet (48) and Claude Haiku (48) answering the requests in scripts/general-requests-holdout.json: the same six genres as ai-general, eight new topics. Written after the 0.2.0 general entries were chosen. Its results were read during the 0.3.0 review rounds, so it is no longer a clean held-out estimate; ai-multi-holdout and ai-detailed-holdout are. Each row records the resolved model id and the system prompt, which tells the model to ignore the account email in its context.

corpora.name: ai-multi-holdout
corpora.what: Six models answering plain one-line requests from scripts/multi-requests.json: seven genres (blog post, email to friends, short essay, local newspaper article, Instagram post, short report, and a long article of about 800 words) on eight everyday topics that appear in no other corpus. Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) answered all 56 requests each (224 texts). OpenAI GPT-5.5 (gpt-5.5-2026-04-23) answered the six short genres on the first topic (6 texts) and GPT-5.4 mini (gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17) the six short genres on the first four topics (24 texts). Sent through the OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages APIs by scripts/generate-api.mjs with no system prompt, default sampling and a 16,000 token limit: the models saw only the request and never a pattern list. Each row records the generator, provider, resolved model id, the exact request and the stop reason. Made after the lists of this release were final, never used to choose or tune an entry, and measured once.
corpora.caveats: OpenAI is kept small for budget: 30 of 254 texts, two models, no long form, so the GPT rows show direction only. Every reply ended normally (stop or end_turn) and is at least 200 characters long. The Claude rows were checked for the right language, personal data, refusals and duplicates. The Italian OpenAI rows come from a first pass of the same 2026-11-05 run, with the same requests and models; that pass also covered more topics, and the rows outside the design above were dropped so the four languages match. No row was read before the lists were final. Email addresses, web addresses and phone numbers that could belong to a real person or business were replaced after generation with example.* addresses and placeholder numbers, in the requests and in the replies alike.

corpora.name: ai-detailed-holdout
corpora.what: Realistic requests with concrete facts, as people type them to a chat assistant: 56 scenarios (eight per genre, the same seven genres as ai-multi-holdout, outlined in scripts/detailed-scenarios.md), each written twice in the language, as a short request (style A, one or two sentences) and a careful one (style B, with audience, tone, length and the facts as notes), in scripts/detailed-requests/it.json. Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) answered all 112 requests each, through the Anthropic Message Batches API (scripts/generate-api.mjs batch) with no system prompt, default sampling and a 16,000 token limit. All requests are set in Italy. Each row records the generator, resolved model id, style, scenario, the exact request and the stop reason. Made after the lists of this release were final, never used to choose or tune an entry, and measured once.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only. The requests were written for this study by a model that did not see the pattern lists, following the scenario outline; names, places, addresses and contact details in them are invented. Every reply ended with end_turn and was checked for the right language, personal data, refusals and duplicates. Email addresses, web addresses and phone numbers that could belong to a real person or business were replaced after generation with example.* addresses and placeholder numbers, in the requests and in the replies alike.
